questions.q: How does medallion architecture relate to Foundations' raw/cleansed/curated zones?
options: It's the same three-layer idea, renamed bronze/silver/gold, now made concrete with Delta tables
It's a completely unrelated concept specific only to Databricks
It replaces the need for any data organization at all
It only applies to streaming data, never batch data
questions.explain: Raw maps to Bronze, Cleansed maps to Silver, Curated maps to Gold.

questions.q: What question does the Silver layer answer?
options: What's the clean, trustworthy version of this data? — the result of null-handling, deduplication, and type-casting
What did we actually receive, unmodified? — a permanent record for reprocessing
What does the business need to see, pre-aggregated for a dashboard?
Silver doesn't answer any particular question; it's purely a staging area
questions.explain: Bronze answers "what did we receive?"; Gold answers "what does the business need?"

questions.q: Why does data flow bronze -> silver -> gold in one direction only?
options: So anyone can trace a number in a gold table backward through silver to the exact bronze rows it came from — a gold table is never the source for silver
Because Delta tables physically cannot be read in reverse
Because Unity Catalog enforces this direction technically
There's actually no real constraint on direction; it's just a common convention with no benefit
questions.explain: This predictability is itself part of the design's value for tracing and reprocessing.

questions.q: Why does Bronze keep data "exactly as received," unmodified?
options: It's a permanent, unaltered record, useful for reprocessing if a later step turns out to be wrong
Because Delta tables cannot be modified once written
Bronze data is deleted after Silver is built, so it must be complete first
Bronze is only used for testing, never for real production pipelines
questions.explain: This mirrors exactly why Foundations' raw zone existed — a safety net for correcting later mistakes.

questions.q: What does the Gold layer typically contain?
options: Business-level aggregates, pre-shaped for a specific dashboard or report
The exact same content as Bronze, just renamed
Only raw, untyped data with no cleaning applied
A backup copy of the Silver layer with no changes
questions.explain: Gold is shaped for direct business consumption, not for a data engineer's own exploration like Silver is.
